# 1. Project Overview

This project investigates the relationship between vehicle weight and fuel efficiency. The main research question is whether heavier vehicles tend to have lower fuel efficiency compared to lighter vehicles.

The analysis will use the built-in `mtcars` dataset in R, which contains information about 32 different automobiles.

# 2. Project Goals

The main goals of this project are:

- Explore the relationship between vehicle weight and fuel efficiency.
- Organize and summarize vehicle data using R.
- Create visualizations to identify possible patterns.
- Calculate the correlation between vehicle weight and miles per gallon (MPG).
- Interpret the results and determine whether vehicle weight is associated with fuel consumption.

# 3. Resources Consulted

The following resources will support the project:

1. [ComputingII GitHub Repository](https://github.com/nmalmberg/ComputingII) – Course materials and examples related to computing and data analysis.
2. [R Documentation](https://www.r-project.org/) – Information about the R programming language.
3. [R mtcars Dataset Documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/datasets/html/mtcars.html) – Information about the automobile dataset.
4. [R Statistical Functions](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/cor.html) – Documentation for calculating correlations.

# 4. Initial Progress and Data Exploration

The initial stage of the project focuses on loading the dataset, examining its structure, and identifying the variables needed for the analysis.

```{r}
# Load the built-in automobile dataset
data(mtcars)

# Display the first six observations
head(mtcars)

# Examine the structure of the dataset
str(mtcars)
```

The variables of interest are:

- `wt`: Vehicle weight (measured in 1,000 pounds).
- `mpg`: Fuel efficiency (miles per gallon).

## 4.1 Descriptive Statistics

The following code calculates basic descriptive statistics for vehicle weight and fuel efficiency.

```{r}
# Summary statistics for selected variables
summary(mtcars[, c("wt", "mpg")])
```

## 4.2 Data Visualization

A scatterplot will be used to explore the relationship between vehicle weight and fuel efficiency.

```{r}
# Create a scatterplot
plot(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg,
     main = "Vehicle Weight vs. Fuel Efficiency",
     xlab = "Vehicle Weight (1,000 lbs)",
     ylab = "Miles Per Gallon (MPG)",
     pch = 19)

# Add a trend line
abline(lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars))
```

## 4.3 Correlation Analysis

The Pearson correlation coefficient will be calculated to measure the strength and direction of the relationship between vehicle weight and fuel efficiency.

```{r}
# Calculate Pearson correlation
cor(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)

# Perform a correlation test
cor.test(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
```

# 5. Preliminary Expectations

Based on the research question, heavier vehicles are expected to have lower miles per gallon. The scatterplot and correlation analysis will help evaluate this expectation.

The initial analysis will provide a foundation for further investigation and interpretation.

# 6. Next Steps

Future work will include:

- Interpreting the statistical results.
- Examining possible outliers and unusual observations.
- Exploring additional variables that may influence fuel efficiency.
- Improving the visualizations.
- Preparing a final summary of the findings.

# 7. Initial Findings

The `mtcars` dataset contains 32 automobile observations. Initial examination of the data shows a negative relationship between vehicle weight and fuel efficiency.

The Pearson correlation between weight and miles per gallon is approximately -0.868. This indicates a strong negative association: heavier vehicles generally have lower fuel efficiency.

The initial findings support the project's research question and provide a foundation for further statistical analysis.

# 8. Conclusion of Progress Report

The project has established its research question, identified a suitable dataset, and developed initial R code for descriptive statistics, visualization, and correlation analysis. The next stage will focus on executing the analysis and interpreting the results in greater detail.
